questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country where I could learn Spanish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to get information on how to select courses and the different deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You received all information on e-mail and were also able to book a timeslot with the coordinator. Furthermore, there were two introduction meetings in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the apps Badi and Idealista to find a place. It was quite easy and I did find a place before I arrived in Barcelona.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a bit more pricy to live off campus but totally worth it if you want to get the full experience of Barcelona.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received all information on e-mail. I had to register in their online system to get my own user. Also, I had to apply for courses before I arrived. However, the first week you could try out multiple courses and finally select after.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was very helpful with the first week where you can try out different courses and talk to the professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wished for. However, it was not possible to get solely English courses so you need to be able to speak a certain level of Spanish even though the university does not require any language test.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to try out different courses once you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Two of the courses were a bit of a repetition of previous courses I had taken at home so they were not that difficult and reminded more of a BA level. The third was at a high level but this one was also in Spanish. It seemed liked the most interesting courses was in Spanish.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of assignments during the semester and midterm exams. They required active participation during the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. European Integration
2. Socio-political Marketing
3. Arab World

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course Arab World was super interesting and at a high level. however, this one was in Spanish so you do need a certain level of Spanish to be able to follow the course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs. However, we were able to go on a lot of trips in the weekends which were more costly but also worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is a lot more cheap to live in Barcelona than Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of sport activities on campus and it is super cheap to get a membership. However, the classes are often always full.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the fitness center where all the sport activities are.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you get the metrocard for 6 zones (costs 40 euros for 3 months), you can for free visit places such as Sitges, Montserrat and some of Costa Brava. Would highly recommend!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find it challenge.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Barcelona as a city just have it all! Beautiful nature and a vibrant city life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You need to have a certain level of Spanish to be able to follow courses for 30 ECTS.
2. You should get the metrocard for 6 zones so you are able to visit all the beautiful places near Barcelona for free
3. Find housing by yourself in Barcelona. It is a bit more pricy but very much worth it! Use apps such as Badi and Idealista

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a city as Barcelona for 4 months! it is just the best city with such a nice culture :)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any great challenges.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
